verification.description: AniimoDex is an unofficial fan resource. We publish only fields that can be traced to a named official source, and we label unknowns instead of guessing.

verification.tiersMapping: The tiers above describe where a claim comes from. Every claim below is labelled with one of three evidence levels: official, community or unknown. Official Wiki and official storefront findings count as official, while post-launch player observations count as community.
verification.claimsDescription: Every claim this site relies on is recorded here with the evidence level we could actually reach. A claim with no first-party source stays marked unknown instead of being presented as a fact.

catchTool.title: Aniimo Catch Rate Calculator
catchTool.subtitle: Estimate a catch chance from the officially published Aniimo probability formula.
catchTool.sourceNote: Every coefficient on this page comes from the official Aniimo probability disclosure checked on 2026-09-18. The result is still an estimate based on the conditions you select because per-species template rates are not published.
catchTool.templateCaveatBody: The official disclosure states that the base rate is decided by each Aniimo template and is not derived from level. Those per-species template rates are not published, so this calculator estimates from the region stage and evolution stage you select instead of claiming an exact species value.
catchTool.defeatedNote: The defeated rule only multiplies the death base rate, the cube and the status coefficient, using the published 6% death rate for common bosses.
catchTool.playerBonusHelp: The official formula folds your character's base catch bonus into the base rate as (1 + bonus). Leave it at 0% if you do not know your value.
catchTool.cubeRemoteMass: Remote big white ball (mass outbreak target)
catchTool.cubeGuaranteedNote: This cube always succeeds as long as the target is catchable.
catchTool.hpHelp: The HP coefficient only applies in battle. The official table is discrete, so no value between those steps is interpolated.
catchTool.backstrikeHelp: A backstrike only applies outside battle, with a standard cube, and when the server confirms it. The big white ball never receives this bonus.
catchTool.statusRuleNote: Official rule: when any status is below 1x the lowest coefficient is used; otherwise the highest is used.
catchTool.statusHundredX: Deep sleep / nectar gathering (some special stuns)
catchTool.statusUncatchable: Rampage / bubble barrier / corrupted / already owned
catchTool.resultUncatchable: This status makes the target uncatchable while it lasts.
catchTool.doubleCheckNote: A standard cube on a normal target is resolved as two separate checks, each using the square root of the final rate. The combined chance still equals the final rate shown here.
catchTool.strategyBackstrike: Attack from behind outside battle with a standard cube to add the 1.5x backstrike coefficient.
catchTool.strategyHp: Lower the target's HP before throwing: the coefficient is 2x at 0% HP but only 0.8x at full HP.
catchTool.strategyStatus: Apply a status effect. Deep sleep, nectar gathering and some special stuns reach a 100x coefficient.
catchTool.strategyLevel: The level difference matters a lot: 11 levels above your character drops the coefficient to 0.8x, and 15 or more drops it to 0.1x.
catchTool.strategyCube: A stronger cube multiplies everything: advanced is 1.5x, and swift, tracking and super cubes are 2x.
catchTool.referenceBody: These are the published values the calculator uses. You choose the region stage and evolution stage yourself, because the per-species template rate is not part of the disclosure.

getting-started.title: Aniimo Beginner Guide: 8 Decisions to Make Before You Spend Resources
getting-started.subtitle: A source-checked starting checklist for downloads, team roles, catching, evolution and multiplayer.
getting-started.lead: Start with decisions that can be checked against official data: use an official download, separate exploration abilities from combat roles, improve known catch factors and verify an evolution before committing resources. This guide does not invent a best starter, leveling route or spending priority.

body.c: 1. Check your platform, region and account first

Use the official Aniimo website or the verified Steam, PlayStation, Xbox and Epic listings. Store availability, mobile timing and account features can vary by platform and region, so confirm the live button before downloading or paying.
2. Confirm PC requirements before installing

The Epic Games Store publishes official minimum and recommended Windows specifications, including CPU, memory, GPU, DirectX and storage. Compare those requirements with your device instead of relying on an unverified compatibility list.
3. Do not choose a starter from an unsupported tier list

The official Wiki publishes element, role, stage and mobility fields, but those labels do not prove which Aniimo is strongest. Choose by the activity you need: damage, break, support, sustain, healing or an exploration ability.
4. Treat combat role and exploration ability separately
A role describes a combat function, while mobility and Twine fields help with traversal or interaction. Check both fields in the Dex before building a team around one label.
5. Improve only the catch factors that are confirmed

The official formula confirms that cube type, level difference, target HP, a valid backstrike and special status can change catch probability. AniimoDex does not assign a precise species percentage when the required template base rate is unpublished.
6. Verify the evolution family before spending

AniimoDex can show evolution-family relationships from the official index. Exact level, quest, item and resource requirements are not assumed unless an official source or reproducible test confirms them.
7. Separate multiplayer from cross-save

Steam confirms multiplayer, online co-op and cross-platform multiplayer, but that does not by itself confirm every platform pairing or cross-save behavior. Check the crossplay guide before planning progress across devices.
8. Be precise about rare forms

The official probability disclosure publishes Sparkling-related rates and the official data identifies form information where available. Community claims about Umbral eggs, guaranteed outcomes or evolution behavior remain unconfirmed until independently verified.

Still under verification: an optimal leveling path, home-base priority, Nurture guarantees, Egg Heist efficiency routes and a universal best team. Use community discussion to discover questions, not as proof of an answer.

what-is-aniimo.title: What Is Aniimo? Gameplay, Twine and Open-World Features
what-is-aniimo.subtitle: An official-source overview of Aniimo and how its core gameplay works.
what-is-aniimo.lead: Aniimo is a free-to-play creature-catching open-world RPG from Pawprint Studio. Players explore Idyll, capture Aniimo, Twine with collected creatures and take part in solo, multiplayer and competitive activities.

body.c: What kind of game is Aniimo?

Official store descriptions call Aniimo a next-generation creature-catching open-world RPG. Its core loop combines exploration, collecting creatures, using their abilities, solving puzzles and taking part in real-time battles and challenges.
What does Twine mean in Aniimo?

Twine lets a Pathfinder become an Aniimo they have collected and use that creature’s abilities. Official examples include gliding, diving and burrowing to explore, solve puzzles, battle and overcome environmental challenges.
How does catching work?

Official store text says players catch Aniimo with Aniipods, can set traps and must time catches. Creatures may appear according to environment, weather, phenomena and time of day. The official probability disclosure now publishes catch formulas and modifiers, while per-creature base templates still require mapping.
Does Aniimo have multiplayer?
Yes. Steam lists multiplayer, PvP, online co-op and cross-platform multiplayer. Xbox describes Egg Heist as a real-time PVEVP activity for three-player teams, alongside solo and multiplayer play.
Who makes Aniimo?
Steam lists Pawprint Studio as both developer and publisher.
Is Aniimo a Pokemon-style game?

Both games involve collecting creatures, but Aniimo's official identity is its own open-world RPG built around Twine transformations, real-time catching and combat, multiplayer activities and exploration. It should not be treated as a Pokemon title or official spin-off.
This overview separates verified official features from dex stats, type multipliers and per-creature catch templates that remain under review.

is-aniimo-a-gacha-game.title: Is Aniimo Pay to Win or Gacha? Monetization Explained
is-aniimo-a-gacha-game.subtitle: What official sources confirm about free play, in-game purchases, random acquisition and paid progression.
is-aniimo-a-gacha-game.lead: Aniimo is free to play and contains in-game purchases. The official sources registered by AniimoDex do not provide enough complete pricing, probability, progression-speed or competitive-impact data to prove that the game is pay to win, so this page separates confirmed facts from open questions.

body.c: Is Aniimo pay to win?

Not enough verified evidence is available for a defensible yes or no. Official storefronts confirm a free base game and in-game purchases, but they do not quantify how spending changes progression speed, combat power, competitive access or the time needed to obtain an Aniimo.
Is Aniimo officially described as a gacha game?

No. The official website and storefront listings describe a free-to-play creature-catching open-world RPG and disclose in-game purchases, but they do not use the gacha label. That wording alone does not prove that every random or paid acquisition mechanic is absent.
What can be obtained or improved without paying?
The base game is listed as free to play on verified PC and console storefronts.
Catching, open-world exploration, Twine and multiplayer are presented as core gameplay rather than separately purchased modes.
The official catch disclosure publishes free gameplay coefficients for HP, level difference, backstrike and status effects.
The official site has listed launch rewards and free catching items, but current account eligibility and claim windows must be checked separately.
What paid systems are officially confirmed?

Steam, PlayStation, Xbox and Google Play disclose in-game purchases. The registered sources do not provide a complete current catalog of prices, passes, currencies, paid Aniimo acquisition, duplicate conversion or progression boosts, so AniimoDex does not label any specific purchase essential or good value.
Are catch rates or rare forms sold?

The official probability disclosure publishes catch coefficients and sparkling-style probabilities, including several cube types. It does not by itself establish which items are paid-only, how much they cost, or whether a player must buy them. Probability data and store monetization must not be treated as the same claim.
What would change the pay-to-win assessment?

head: Question
Current evidence status
rows: Can money directly buy stronger stats?
Can paid items skip meaningful progression?
Are Aniimo obtained through paid random draws?
Not confirmed by official listings used here

body.c: How should a player decide whether to spend?
Play the free progression loop first and identify the exact limit you are trying to remove.
Check the live in-game price, contents, probability disclosure and expiry before paying.
Do not infer value from a launch reward, community tier list or another region's price.
Keep platform receipts and avoid repeated purchases while account or server progress is unclear.
AniimoDex will update this assessment only when official rules or reproducible live-version tests can separate convenience, random acquisition and direct power.

aniimo-twine-explained.subtitle: Twine lets Pathfinders become collected Aniimo and use their abilities.
aniimo-twine-explained.lead: Twine is one of Aniimo's defining systems: a Pathfinder can become an Aniimo they have collected and use that creature's abilities in exploration, puzzles and battles.

body.c: What does Twine mean in Aniimo?
Official descriptions say players can Twine with collected Aniimo. Examples include gliding, diving and burrowing through the world while using creature-specific abilities.
What is Twine used for?
Exploring terrain and reaching new areas
Solving environmental puzzles
Using Aniimo abilities in real-time combat
Which Aniimo have each Twine ability?
A complete official ability-by-creature list has not been published in the sources used here. Community dex mappings remain under review.

aniimo-catching-guide.title: How to Catch Aniimo: Aniipods, Traps and Spawn Conditions
aniimo-catching-guide.subtitle: An official-source guide to the catching mechanics confirmed so far.
aniimo-catching-guide.lead: Official store descriptions confirm that players use Aniipods, traps and timing to catch Aniimo, while environment, weather, phenomena and time of day affect appearances.

body.c: How does catching work in Aniimo?
Players explore habitats, encounter Aniimo and use Aniipods to catch them. Official text also mentions setting traps and choosing the right timing.
What affects where Aniimo appear?
Environment and habitat
Weather
Special phenomena
Time of day
How is the Aniimo catch rate calculated?

The official probability disclosure now publishes separate formulas for out-of-combat, in-combat and defeated targets. Published factors include the regional base rate, character catch bonus, cube type, level difference, target HP, backstrike and status effects.
What catch bonuses are officially confirmed?

Examples include Advanced Cubes at ×1.5, several higher cubes at ×2, a valid out-of-combat backstrike at ×1.5, BREAK at ×1.5 and ordinary sleep or stun at ×2. Some states force success or make a target impossible to catch.
A per-creature percentage still requires that Aniimo's configured base-rate group and current encounter conditions. AniimoDex does not guess an unmapped template rate.
Three official-coefficient examples

head: Scenario
Published factors
Relative multiplier before the unknown base rate
rows: Out-of-battle standard cube with a valid backstrike
In battle at 0% HP with ordinary sleep
Target is 15 or more levels above the character

body.c: These examples compare published modifiers only. They are not final catch percentages because the Aniimo template base rate, region stage, evolution stage, cube and any other active factors must also be known.

aniimo-team-composition.title: Aniimo Team Composition: Roles, Elements and Mobility
aniimo-team-composition.subtitle: A functional team-building guide built on published role, element and mobility fields, and not a tier list.
aniimo-team-composition.lead: AniimoDex does not publish strength rankings. This page explains what each officially published role label covers, how element labels and mobility coverage shape a team, and how to choose a starting Aniimo from what you actually want to do.

body.c: Does AniimoDex publish a tier list?

No. The official Wiki index publishes a role label and one or more element labels per Aniimo, and neither field identifies which Aniimo performs best. A ranking would be an opinion, so this page stays on team functions.
How many Aniimo carry each published role?
What does each published role cover?
DPS - the index label for damage-dealing Aniimo, and by far the largest group.
Break - the index label tied to breaking a target. The official catch disclosure confirms a BREAK state adds a x1.5 catch coefficient and that the break catch bonus reaches x3.
Support - the index label for supportive Aniimo that contribute team effects.
Regen - the index label for sustain and recovery over time.
Heal - the index label for healing Aniimo and the smallest group, with only 7 indexed entries.

These descriptions come from the published labels and, where noted, the official probability disclosure. The detail snapshot publishes skill names and descriptions, but not a complete set of cooldowns, damage values, progression costs or balance data.
How do element labels fit into a team?

Element labels are verified official data, and 13 of the 92 indexed Aniimo carry more than one element. The matchup multipliers in the type chart tool, however, are a community-compiled reference rather than official data, so use element labels to check that your team covers different elements rather than to assume a guaranteed counter.
Why does mobility matter for a team?

Mobility is the field ability used for traversal or environmental interaction, and 48 of the 92 indexed Aniimo publish one, across 19 distinct ability names. These descriptions can help you compare field functions, but the source does not map them to specific required routes or locations.
What should a new player choose first?
Choose by what you want to do rather than by which Aniimo looks strongest.
To explore: shortlist Aniimo that publish a mobility ability, because fewer than half of the index carries that field.

To catch efficiently: consult the published status and backstrike coefficients, then verify which Aniimo can apply the relevant state in your current version. The source does not compare those teams with damage-focused teams.
To play co-op: look at Support, Regen and Heal, which are the three smallest published groups at 18, 10 and 7 indexed Aniimo.
What can this page not tell you?

It cannot rank Aniimo or recommend one fixed team. The registered sources include published stats and skill descriptions, but they do not provide enough complete cooldown, damage, progression-cost and version-balance data for a defensible strength ranking.
Roles and elements describe what an Aniimo is for, not how strong it is. This page stays on the functional side of that line.

aniimo-forms-explained.title: Aniimo Prismana, Umbral and Sparkling Forms Explained
aniimo-forms-explained.subtitle: What official sources confirm about Prismana and Sparkling styles, and what remains unverified about Umbral eggs.
aniimo-forms-explained.lead: Prismana, Sparkling and Umbral are active player searches, but they are not interchangeable labels. The official Wiki indexes Prismana as a morphology entry, the probability disclosure publishes Sparkling styles, and the registered official data does not yet define Umbral eggs or their evolution rules.

body.c: Prismana vs Sparkling vs Umbral: what is confirmed?

head: Term
Confirmed source status
What AniimoDex can safely say
rows: 21 of 92 indexed Aniimo list a Prismana Form; its gameplay effects are not defined in the registered official source
Normal, Dazzling and Shadow style probabilities are published for specific obtaining methods
Not defined in the registered official fields

body.c: What form data is officially published?

The official Wiki detail snapshot records a morphology list for each Aniimo. Across the 92 indexed Aniimo, 19 distinct form names appear, and they fall into three groups: every entry has a Basic Form, 21 entries also have a Prismana Form, and the rest are named after a region or a weather state.
What is a Prismana Form?

Prismana Form is the official name used in the morphology list, and 21 of the 92 indexed Aniimo publish one. Community coverage describes Prismana as changing an Aniimo's element rather than its stats, but the official Wiki sources used here do not say what a Prismana Form changes, so AniimoDex keeps that statement at community level.
What is an Umbral Aniimo or Umbral Egg?

Umbral is a current community search term, but it does not appear as a morphology category or Sparkling style in the official datasets registered for this page. AniimoDex therefore cannot yet confirm where an Umbral Egg comes from, whether its hatch is random, what a Sparkling Cube changes, or whether Umbral status survives evolution.

Conflicting community replies are useful for identifying questions, not for confirming a mechanic. Umbral instructions will be added only after an official rule or a documented, reproducible test is available.
What are region forms?

The remaining 17 form names are tied to a place or a weather state, such as Highland Form, Snowfield Form, Sea of Flowers Form, Rainstorm Form and Nighttime Form. The official index records the names only and does not publish what differs between them.
Are sparkling forms in the same list?

No. No sparkling entry appears anywhere in the official morphology list. The sparkling styles are published separately in the official probability disclosure, so the two systems should not be treated as one field.
Which sparkling styles are officially published?

head: How it is obtained
Normal

rows: Sparkling Cube on a wild Aniimo

Sparkling Color to change the style

body.c: In both Sparkling Cube routes the normal style is 99%, which means the rare outcomes are the Dazzling style at 1%, or the Shadow style at 1% on Egg Heist eggs, rather than sparkling itself.
What do sparkling styles change?
The official disclosure publishes only how each style is obtained. It does not state whether a sparkling style changes stats, elements or roles, so AniimoDex does not claim any of those effects.
Why does the Dex not show stats per form?

The official sources used by AniimoDex do not publish per-form stats, elements, roles or abilities. The Dex therefore lists each form name with its category instead of filling the gaps with estimated numbers.
Use Prismana for an official morphology entry, Sparkling for the separately published style system, and Umbral only as an unverified community term until stronger evidence is available.

aniimo-multiplayer.lead: Aniimo supports solo and multiplayer activities. Steam lists PvP, online co-op and cross-platform multiplayer, while Xbox describes the three-player Egg Heist PVEVP mode.

body.c: Does Aniimo have co-op?
Yes. Steam lists online co-op and multiplayer. The final availability of specific activities may depend on platform, account and launch version.
Does Aniimo have PvP?
Steam lists PvP, and Xbox describes Egg Heist as a real-time PVEVP activity where three-player teams compete while facing environmental threats.
Is Aniimo cross-platform?
Steam lists cross-platform multiplayer. Official sources checked here do not yet explain every cross-save, account-linking or platform-combination detail.

aniimo-egg-heist.title: Aniimo Egg Heist Guide: PVEVP and Shadow Sparkling Odds
aniimo-egg-heist.subtitle: The official facts about Egg Heist, its three-player format and the published Shadow Sparkling probability.
aniimo-egg-heist.lead: Egg Heist is an official real-time PVEVP activity for three-player teams. Xbox confirms the mode format, while Aniimo's probability disclosure separately confirms how an Egg Heist egg differs in the Sparkling style table. Exact unlock requirements, rewards and efficient routes remain unverified here.

body.c: What is Egg Heist in Aniimo?

Xbox describes Egg Heist as a real-time PVEVP activity. Teams of three compete while also dealing with environmental threats, so the published description combines player-versus-environment and player-versus-player pressure.
How many players are on an Egg Heist team?

The official Xbox description specifies three-player teams. It does not establish whether matchmaking fills every missing position, whether a smaller party can queue, or which platforms can invite one another in this activity.
Does Egg Heist support cross-platform play?

Steam lists cross-platform multiplayer for Aniimo as a product feature, but the registered official sources do not document every supported platform pairing or confirm Egg Heist-specific crossplay behavior. Cross-save is a separate question and also remains incompletely documented.
What is special about an Egg Heist egg?

The official probability disclosure distinguishes an Egg Heist egg from other eggs in its Sparkling style table. When a Sparkling Cube is used on an Egg Heist egg, the published outcomes are 99% Normal Sparkling, 0% Dazzling Sparkling and 1% Shadow Sparkling.

This table describes the style outcome after the listed Sparkling Cube use. It does not prove that an Egg Heist egg is guaranteed to contain a particular Aniimo, that a Shadow style changes stats, or that any claimed farming route is optimal.
What should players verify before entering?
The mode is currently available on the platform and server being used
All team members are on a compatible game version
The in-game activity screen shows the current access requirement and reward rules
Any Sparkling item description matches the official probability disclosure before use
What is still unverified?

AniimoDex does not currently publish an unlock level, quest path, match duration, reward table, best team, fastest egg route or guaranteed hatch result. Those claims require a current official rule or a documented test with platform, server and game version.
Published now: mode type, team size and the Egg Heist row in the official Sparkling table. Held back: unlock steps, optimal routes, reward efficiency and guaranteed egg outcomes.

Does Aniimo have cross-save or cross-progression?

Choose a primary platform until Pawprint Studio publishes account-linking details. Do not assume that a shared multiplayer session also transfers saves, achievements, purchases or premium currency.

Only after the live version exposes complete skills, stats, progression and repeatable combat results. Every recommendation will name the tested game version and will be revised after balance changes.
